rollback: npx wrangler delete --name uk-income-tax-salary-mcp (brand-new worker, no prior version)
fixture_basis: gov.uk worked examples: NI GBP 1,000/week -> 58.66; GBP 35,000 -> 20% on 22,430; Plan 1 GBP 42,000 -> 1,359; several-plan and postgraduate rules; relief at source 12,000 with 10,000 taxed at 40% -> 2,000 extra relief. Others: hand arithmetic on HMRC employer tables (rUK and Scottish 2025/26 + 2026/27 band splits, taper at 110k/125,140, marginal 62% / 69.5% / 37%, salary sacrifice, K/BR/SD1 codes, Plan 5).
stdio_local_ok: initialize + tools/list + 4/4 tools/call OK, plus a Plan 5 2025/26 error case returning isError with a clear message (node dist/stdio.js)
unannounced: none: 2026/27 Scottish bands and all 2026/27 student loan thresholds are published. Plan 5 in 2025/26 is marked not_set (HMRC 2025 to 2026 employer table lists no Plan 5 threshold) and the tool refuses with a message rather than guess.
open_issues: Annual calculation only; payroll per-period rounding (monthly NI/student loan thresholds) can differ by a few pounds. Stated in every result.
Not modelled: net pay arrangement pensions, employer pension, benefits in kind, HICBC, K-code 50% overriding limit, savings/dividends. Listed in README Limitations.

Site ukmoneycalc.com engine values match gov.uk for 2026/27 (checked src/consts.ts); site comment says Plan 5 'unchanged' although HMRC's 2025/26 employer table lists no Plan 5 threshold. Cosmetic, no number differs.
GitHub search rank not measured (search API rate-limited, not called per instructions).

content.text:
Scottish income tax for 2026/27, on gross pay with the standard £12,570 allowance: starter 19% from £12,571 to £16,537; basic 20% from £16,538 to £29,526; intermediate 21% from £29,527 to £43,662; higher 42% from £43,663 to £75,000; advanced 45% from £75,001 to £125,140; top 48% from £125,141 up. The allowance falls by £1 for every £2 over £100,000 and is gone at £125,140. Employee NI is 8% from £12,570 to £50,270 and 2% above. Student loan thresholds: Plan 1 £26,900, Plan 2 £29,385, Plan 4 £33,795, Plan 5 £25,000, Postgraduate £21,000.

Estimate for one employment, worked out on annual figures. Payroll works per pay period, so a payslip can differ by a few pounds. Not tax advice.

content.text:
At £110,000 in 2026/27 (Scotland) the marginal rate on the next £100 is 69.5%: income tax 67.5%, National Insurance 2%. This income is inside the £100,000 to £125,140 taper: each extra £1 also removes £0.50 of Personal Allowance, so the 45% band works out at 67.5%. You keep £30.50 of each extra £100.

tools.name: calculate_uk_take_home
tools.title: UK take-home pay
tools.description: Calculates UK take-home pay for an employee in tax year 2025/26 or 2026/27 from HMRC's published rates: income tax by band (England, Wales and NI, or the six Scottish bands incl. the 2026/27 Scottish starter and basic bands), employee Class 1 National Insurance (8% / 2%), student loan repayments (Plan 1, 2, 4, 5 and Postgraduate, with 2026/27 thresholds), and pension by salary sacrifice or relief at source. Applies the Personal Allowance taper above £100,000 (£1 per £2, the 60% trap) and reads tax codes such as 1257L, S1257L, K475, BR and D0. Returns net pay a year, a month and a week. Figures copied from gov.uk and HMRC in Oct 2026.

gross_salary.description: Annual gross salary in pounds (GBP), before any deductions.

tax_year.description: UK tax year, 6 April to 5 April. 2025/26 or 2026/27 (default 2026/27).

region.description: Where you live for tax. england, wales, northern_ireland (same bands) or scotland (six Scottish bands). Default england, or taken from an S or C tax code.

tax_code.description: PAYE tax code, default 1257L. Supports nnnnL/M/N/T, S and C prefixes, K codes, BR, D0, D1, SBR, SD0-SD3, 0T, NT and W1/M1/X suffixes.

pension_method.description: relief_at_source (you pay 80%, provider adds 20%, higher-rate relief claimed back) or salary_sacrifice (cuts pay before tax, NI and student loan). Default salary_sacrifice if a pension is given.

pension_percent.description: Employee pension contribution as a percent of gross salary, e.g. 5. For relief at source this is the gross (grossed-up) contribution.

pension_amount.description: Employee pension contribution in pounds a year (gross). Use this OR pension_percent.

student_loan_plans.description: Student loan plans you repay: plan_1, plan_2, plan_4 (Scotland), plan_5, postgraduate. Several are allowed, as gov.uk describes.

ni_category.description: National Insurance category letter, default A. C = over State Pension age (no employee NI).

tools.name: get_uk_tax_bands
tools.title: UK income tax bands and thresholds
tools.description: Returns the official UK income tax bands for 2025/26 or 2026/27, for England, Wales and Northern Ireland or for Scotland (starter 19%, basic 20%, intermediate 21%, higher 42%, advanced 45%, top 48%), both as taxable-income bands from HMRC's employer tables and as gross-salary bands with the standard £12,570 allowance. Also returns the £100,000 allowance taper, Class 1 NI thresholds and employee rates by category letter, and student loan thresholds for each plan. A figure that is not published is marked unannounced, never guessed. Copied from gov.uk and HMRC in Oct 2026.

region.description: england, wales, northern_ireland, england_wales_ni or scotland.

annotations.title: UK income tax bands and thresholds

tools.name: compare_salaries
tools.title: Compare UK salaries after tax
tools.description: Compares 1 to 5 UK gross salaries after income tax, National Insurance, student loan and pension for 2025/26 or 2026/27, with the same region, tax code and options for each. Shows net pay a year, month and week, effective and marginal rates, and how much of each pay rise you keep compared with the first salary. Shows when a rise lands in the £100,000 to £125,140 Personal Allowance taper (60% in England, 69.5% in Scotland in 2026/27 with NI). Uses HMRC 2025/26 and 2026/27 rates fetched in Oct 2026.

tools.name: marginal_rate_at_income
tools.title: UK marginal tax rate at a salary
tools.description: Returns the true UK marginal rate on the next pounds of salary in 2025/26 or 2026/27: income tax band rate, employee NI and student loan together, plus the Personal Allowance taper between £100,000 and £125,140 that makes it 60% plus NI in England, Wales and NI and 67.5% plus NI in Scotland's advanced band.
